segments.narration_text: One small test was useful. A second team asks to run it too. That sounds like progress, and it may be. It also changes the shape of the work. The first team knew the people, the context, and the reason for every field in its learning plan. The second team receives a template and a sentence about success. Context can disappear between those two moments.

segments.narration_text: Chapter Twenty-Four names five scaling mistakes. A central team can become a bottleneck. Documentation can grow so heavy that people stop testing. The organization can fixate on one tool instead of shared learning. Teams can resist a process they did not help shape. And leaders can expand across the whole organization before the first handoff works. Put those five labels on the checklist and test your own proposal against them.

segments.narration_text: The decision-memory record is where a useful test becomes a reusable asset. Write what the team believed before the test. Link to the source evidence. Record what happened, including contrary observations and limits. State the choice, the person accountable for it, and the condition that would reopen it. Add the date when its context should be checked again. If the decision was to defer, say why.

segments.narration_text: End with a decision about readiness, even if the answer is wait. Choose one neighboring team for a future handoff only after the record survives a dry run. State which safeguards belong to the shared process and which must be set locally. This keeps a successful local experiment from becoming an organization-wide promise by accident.
